thread:
Maya: heads-up — canary after the 13:04 deploy crossed our p95 error threshold (5% rule) in us-west.
Deploy-bot: canary_alert: service=frontend error_rate_p95=6.2% threshold=5% -> action=flag
Liam: seeing the same in logs, 5xx spike from gorouter. quick check: is it only the new model bundle?
Sanjay: yes, the rollout included model v3.2 with the new KV-cache change. dedicated customers still on v3.1.
Maya: proposal: do a "safety-net switch" (route new traffic off v3.2 back to v3.1) instead of full org-wide rollback. lower blast radius.
Julie: agree on safety-net switch, but we need comms. I'll ping support + legal about any customer-facing notes.
Maya: command ready: `deployctl route set --service frontend --from variant=v3.2 --to variant=v3.1 --percent=100 --meta= safety-net-switch`
Liam: +1. If we flip, monitor p95, error-rate, and payload regressions for 15m. set alert for re-escalation.
Deploy-bot: action_started: safety-net-switch initiated by Maya at 1950012358, target=variant:v3.1
Sanjay: note: this won't revert the model in storage, it's just routing. we should pin the rollout PR after confirmation to avoid auto-retry.
Maya: doing pin now: `releasectl pin --component=frontend --version=v3.1 --reason="safety-net switch after canary error"`
Julie: comms draft: "13:04 deploy caused increased errors for a subset of traffic; we routed affected traffic to the previously stable variant (v3.1) while we investigate. Customers may see transient retries. We will post updates at :30 and when resolved." thoughts?
Liam: looks good. add note to mention dedicated customers unaffected.
Maya: switch result at +2m: p95 back to 1.0% and error rate dropped under 1.2% :white_check_mark:
Deploy-bot: action_completed: safety-net-switch completed at 1950012378. metrics: p95=1.03% error_rate_p95=1.15%.
Sanjay: opening a follow-up: PM-INVEST-1481 to track root cause and decide whether to revert model changes in the next patch.
Julie: I'll post the short status update to #customer-comm and tag support. will also add a short note to the release notes: "emergency traffic routing to v3.1 due to canary error spike; investigating".
Liam: add runbook tweak: automatic fallback should be enabled for hosted customers but remain manual for dedicated — we hit confusion there today.
Maya: agreed, filing runbook PR. after 30m monitoring we'll either unpin (if investigation shows false positive) or keep v3.1 and schedule a controlled rollout for v3.2.
Julie: thanks team. I'll close comms loop once support acknowledges.
Liam: I'll keep this thread open until postmortem ticket created and owners assigned.
Deploy-bot: note: next deploy attempts for v3.2 will be blocked until PR #4621 is unblocked by releases.
Maya: acknowledged. good job everyone!
